official.deadline_central_display: No single student deadline: student applications run through the international relations office of the Swiss host institution, which sets its own dates. Institutional accreditation and funding applications go to Movetia annually at the beginning of March for a funding period starting 1 June; Movetia states the next application deadline for institutions is spring 2027, likely under Erasmus+.
official.deadline_note: Movetia publishes no central deadline for individual incoming students. At institutional level, accreditation and funding applications can be submitted annually at the beginning of March and the funding period starts on 1 June. Next deadline for institutions: spring 2027, likely under Erasmus+.
official.application_cycle: SEMP Call 2026 runs from 1 June 2026 to 31 August 2027 (shortened to allow a smooth transition); the next call is expected from spring 2027, likely within Erasmus+
official.status_note: SEMP is the current Swiss solution for higher education mobility. Movetia states the SEMP Call 2026 runs from 1 June 2026 to 31 August 2027, that the next call will likely be launched within Erasmus+, and that detailed information will be published in autumn 2026.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Movetia publishes that students 'do not pay study fees abroad' and lists 'No tuition fees at the host institution' as added value for participants.
official.funding_period: per mobility (varies by duration and country)
benefits: European mobility, incoming: CHF 1,430 to CHF 4,500 depending on duration and country of origin
Worldwide mobility: CHF 1,750 to CHF 5,000 for incoming and outgoing mobility, depending on duration
European mobility grants include CHF 100 for sustainable mobility, paid only when travelling to and from the destination by train, bus or car sharing
For specific needs of individuals with disabilities or physical, mental or chronic illnesses: max. CHF 12,000 (actual costs based on the note of requirements)
No tuition fees at the host institution
Recognition of achievements abroad towards the home degree (ECTS credits or equivalent)
eligibility: Enrolled at a higher education institution (university, university of applied sciences, university of teacher education) or at a college of higher education in Switzerland or abroad, including PhD students
The stay will last between 60 days and 12 months
Home and host institutions have an interinstitutional agreement
Courses followed at the host institution count towards the home degree (ETCS credits or equivalent)
Only Swiss institutions can apply for funding with Movetia; incoming students apply through the Swiss host institution
SEMP grants may be subject to internal criteria of the Swiss institution (for example only mobility within Europe)

Study fees are not charged at the Swiss host institution
CHF 100 sustainable-mobility contribution within European mobility grants, paid only for sustainable travel
Additional special-needs grant up to CHF 12,000 for actual costs arising from a disability or physical, mental or chronic illness
application_method: Incoming student contacts the International Relations Office of the Swiss host institution they plan to attend
The home institution abroad runs the application and nominates the student
The Swiss host institution coordinates the SEMP grant application and pays the grant out
Swiss institutions apply for accreditation with Movetia and submit a funding application, annually at the beginning of March
official.application_route: Apply through your home institution's international office, which nominates you to a partner Swiss institution; the Swiss host institution's International Relations Office then coordinates and pays the SEMP grant.
official.study_mode: Full-time mobility (one or two semesters, or a traineeship of at least 60 days)
official.citizenship_residency: Open to students enrolled at a higher education institution outside Switzerland; no citizenship restriction is published, but mobility must run within an interinstitutional agreement with a Swiss SEMP-accredited institution
official.international_eligibility: Yes: incoming students from abroad are explicitly supported, and traineeships in Switzerland must be organised through a Swiss higher education institution
official.duration: 2 to 12 months per stay (minimum 60 days); one or two semesters for study mobility
official.description: The Swiss-European Mobility Programme (SEMP) is the higher education part of the Swiss Programme for Erasmus+ and supports students, including PhD students, spending one or two semesters or a traineeship at a higher education institution in Switzerland, financed on behalf of the Confederation and the cantons by the national agency Movetia.
official.program_type: Government mobility programme (higher education), Swiss solution to Erasmus+ - incoming mobility

applicant_utility.summary: There is no application you can send to Movetia: for incoming mobility your first email must go to the International Relations Office of the Swiss institution you want to attend, because only that office can submit the SEMP grant and pay it out. Check before anything else that your home university already has an interinstitutional agreement with that Swiss institution, since no agreement means no funding regardless of your grades. Expect the grant to sit somewhere between CHF 1,430 and CHF 4,500 for a European stay, or up to CHF 5,000 for worldwide mobility, and note that your tuition at the Swiss host is waived.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Students already enrolled at a university abroad whose institution has a Swiss partner and who can spare one or two semesters without paying Swiss tuition.
application_readiness_checklist: Email the International Relations Office of your target Swiss institution and ask whether they participate in SEMP, hold an agreement with your home university, and what their internal deadline is
Confirm with your home institution's international office that they will nominate you and that the planned courses will be credited towards your degree
Plan a stay of at least 60 days and no more than 12 months, and check the maximum number of students your destination accepts
Ask the Swiss office whether they restrict SEMP grants to European destinations only, since that internal rule varies by institution
If you qualify for the special-needs grant, start the note of requirements with the Swiss office well before departure
common_rejection_risks: No interinstitutional agreement between your home and the Swiss host institution, which disqualifies the mobility outright
Choosing a Swiss institution that is not SEMP-accredited or simply does not pay out incoming grants
Missing the Swiss host institution's own internal deadline, which is set locally and is not published by Movetia
Planning a stay shorter than 60 days or longer than 12 months
Assuming the grant covers your whole budget: it is travel and accommodation support, not a living allowance for a full Swiss semester
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Swiss cost of living beyond the travel and accommodation contribution, health insurance and any visa fees, plus the CHF 100 sustainable-travel element only arrives if you actually travel by train, bus or car sharing.
document_audit: The note of requirements for a special-needs grant must reflect actual costs and is handled through the Swiss international office, not through Movetia directly
Do not send documents to Movetia at all; the Swiss host institution holds the file
Keep proof that the courses you plan to take will be credited towards your home degree, as this is a published condition
alerts: Switzerland currently runs SEMP instead of Erasmus+ association; Movetia says the next call will likely be launched under Erasmus+ from spring 2027, so the framework and possibly the grant amounts may change for later intakes
The SEMP Call 2026 is shortened to 1 June 2026 - 31 August 2027, which compresses the window in which mobilities can be funded
Each Swiss institution sets its own criteria and deadlines, and some fund only European destinations
Insurance and visa fees are at your own expense
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You approach the Swiss host institution's International Relations Office; your home institution nominates you; the Swiss office submits and pays the grant.
